vera/fatture-xml-check.title: Two files do not always mean two invoices
vera/fatture-xml-check.goal: Read a FatturaPA summary and distinguish invoice bodies, formal anomalies and duplicate candidates.
vera/fatture-xml-check.scenario: The fictional batch contains one valid invoice XML, another copy of that invoice and a truncated XML. The check concerns formal file content; it does not compare invoices with accounting entries.
vera/fatture-xml-check.request: Vera, check this small XML batch and show what needs review.
vera/fatture-xml-check.scope: Formal FatturaPA checks only, without confirming booking, deductibility, payment or VAT treatment.
vera/fatture-xml-check.basis: File count differs from invoice-body count. Supplier, number, date and amount support a duplicate candidate, not automatic deletion.
method: Select client, engagement, batch and year, then import the sources into the managed tutorial case.
Run the current parser and inspect all anomaly and duplicate-group handoff items. Open exact XML when a source fact needs checking.
Present the per-body summary, duplicate candidates and anomaly memo. Keep unreadable files explicitly visible.
vera/fatture-xml-check.result_title: A batch with two issues to review
vera/fatture-xml-check.conclusion: Two readable copies do not automatically represent two economic transactions. The truncated file supplies no reliable extracted invoice record.
vera/fatture-xml-check.check: An anomaly or duplicate candidate does not authorize file deletion or accounting changes. One XML may contain several invoice bodies.
vera/fatture-xml-check.question: Do three received files mean three valid invoices?
vera/fatture-xml-check.answer: No. Count files, readable bodies and anomalies separately. The copy and truncated file need explicit treatment.
vera/fatture-xml-check.practice: Run the packaged XML starter, then a changed copy, and compare the actual anomaly memos.
vera/fatture-xml-check.next: Specify the year and selected batch. Use accounting reconciliation only when that is the requested task.

vera/financial-analysis.title: Understand revenue concentration
vera/financial-analysis.goal: Use a supported financial recipe and interpret its indicator without an automatic risk judgment.
vera/financial-analysis.scenario: A fictional period export contains EUR 100,000 revenue: Alpha 60,000, Beta 25,000 and Gamma 15,000. The professional wants to understand customer dependence, not value the business.
vera/financial-analysis.request: Vera, analyze customer concentration and show the basis of the result.
vera/financial-analysis.scope: The customer_concentration recipe on reviewed historical data. This is not valuation, a rating or an independent accounting-source audit.
vera/financial-analysis.basis: F1 defines this period and scope. It totals EUR 100,000 but supplies no contracts, customer margins or forward-looking evidence.
method: Select the supported recipe that answers the question and qualify sources, period, signs and control total.
Run the package under its reviewed contract and the same engagement context. Use the supported calculations rather than an improvised substitute.
Read indicators and limitations. Connect commentary to metrics and retain any unperformed source checks as such.
vera/financial-analysis.conclusion: The largest customer contributes 60%; the first two contribute 85%. These observations identify commercial questions to investigate.
vera/financial-analysis.check: A large share establishes concentration, not contract fragility or future customer loss. Check scope and total reconciliation.
vera/financial-analysis.question: Does the 60% share tell us the probability of losing revenue?
vera/financial-analysis.answer: No. Contracts, renewals and dependencies need separate evidence. The indicator directs questions but supplies no loss probability.
vera/financial-analysis.practice: Add a fourth customer with EUR 20,000 and check the updated total and shares.
vera/financial-analysis.next: Choose a supported recipe and prepare reviewed accounting sources with period and control totals.

vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.title: Two payments for one posting
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.goal: Reconcile bank and journal data while preserving references, groups and unresolved differences.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.scenario: The fictional journal records EUR 1,200 received for INV-401. The bank statement shows EUR 700 and EUR 500 credits with that reference, plus an EUR 12 fee absent from the supplied journal.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.request: Vera, reconcile these movements and show what remains open.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.scope: Bank-to-journal comparison for one period and currency. It does not verify all open items or authorize automatic postings.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.basis: The common reference supports 700 + 500 against 1,200. The fee has a different purpose and direction and remains separate.
method: Inspect formats and review columns, signs, dates, currency and references using the actual sources.
Run supported matches, including reference-supported groups. Preserve component rows; do not search arbitrary combinations merely to make totals close.
Read matched entries, groups and residuals. Explain the evidence for each link and leave differences and any postings to professional review.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.conclusion: 700 + 500 = EUR 1,200 for INV-401. The EUR 12 bank fee has no counterpart in the supplied journal.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.check: An equal sum does not justify every group. Sign, period, currency and references must remain coherent.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.question: Without references, can we still automatically assign both credits to INV-401?
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.answer: The sum alone does not support the same automatic group. Review the evidence and preserve ambiguity when a sufficient connection is missing.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.practice: Change the second credit to EUR 480 and inspect the residual without inventing another payment.
vera/journal-bank-reconciliation.next: Select journal and statement for the same scope; clarify only mappings that the files cannot resolve.

vera/journal-sampling.title: A reliable population before the sample
vera/journal-sampling.goal: Understand why journal qualification precedes the selection of entries for review.
vera/journal-sampling.scenario: The fictional journal retains original movement IDs, accounts and debit/credit amounts. A value reads '1.200,00', requiring the correct numeric interpretation. A total row is a summary, not another posting to sample.
vera/journal-sampling.request: Vera, prepare this journal and show the sample alongside the population checks.
vera/journal-sampling.scope: Preparation and sampling under the current contract. A selection is not automatically statistically representative or document-vouched.
vera/journal-sampling.basis: IDs and locators come from G1. A physical row number does not replace the original movement identifier.
method: Inspect and review scope, mappings, number format and summary rows before normalization.
Qualify the complete population and verify closure and monetary controls. Apply the reviewed selection method while preserving original identifiers.
Deliver normalized population, diagnostics, sample and assurance companions. Downstream Vouching uses this closed handoff without remapping the source.
vera/journal-sampling.conclusion: The case separates two accounting lines of one movement from a total row. Under the reviewed format, 1.200,00 means EUR 1,200.
vera/journal-sampling.check: A normalized file is not qualified merely because it opens. Wrong mappings can yield plausible but incorrect numbers.
vera/journal-sampling.question: Can we call the movement M-2 because it is on row two?
vera/journal-sampling.answer: No. Preserve M-101 from the source. The row locator helps recover evidence; it does not create movement identity.
vera/journal-sampling.practice: Add an unbalanced line and verify that qualification exposes it before sampling.
vera/journal-sampling.next: Prepare the full export and control totals, then explain the purpose of selection.

vera/management-control-pack.title: Actual versus Budget: read amounts and percentages
vera/management-control-pack.goal: Interpret a management report using reviewed periods, signs and categories.
vera/management-control-pack.scenario: Fictional Arco compares January and February. Actual revenue is EUR 150,000 versus Budget 140,000; included costs are 60,000 versus 59,000. No open-item schedules or later-month forecasts are supplied.
vera/management-control-pack.request: Vera, show where the result differs from Budget in the two closed months.
vera/management-control-pack.scope: A margin comparison on supplied categories. Unsupported sections remain unavailable; no forecast, aging schedule or future months are invented.
vera/management-control-pack.basis: M1 and M2 describe the same two complete months. Category meaning and cost signs are reviewed before comparison.
method: Inspect exports and review roles, columns, categories, signs, currency, period and cutoff. Confirm control totals.
Run the local pack and read metrics and limitations. Show absolute and percentage changes, withholding misleading percentages on zero or negative bases.
Explain the main contributions while separating observations from hypotheses. Optional sections require adequate inputs and commentary remains reviewable.
vera/management-control-pack.conclusion: Extra revenue adds EUR 10,000 and higher costs absorb EUR 1,000. Margin rises from EUR 81,000 to EUR 90,000: +11.11%.
vera/management-control-pack.check: A positive cost change is not favorable. Check comparable periods and categories before explaining a commercial cause.
vera/management-control-pack.question: What do we retain when an item's Budget is zero?
vera/management-control-pack.answer: Retain the EUR difference and mark the percentage unavailable. Do not display infinity or an invented percentage.
vera/management-control-pack.practice: Add a complete month to both exports and rerun with the new cutoff.
vera/management-control-pack.next: Select coherent accounting and Budget exports. Add aging or forecast inputs when they belong to the assignment and are available.

vera/new-client.title: Start a client file without turning gaps into confirmations
vera/new-client.goal: Move from received documents to a professional setup proposal with explicit missing evidence.
vera/new-client.scenario: Fictional Arco Srl supplies a company extract, the representative's ID and a draft engagement letter. The letter is unsigned and the beneficial-ownership declaration is missing. Document preparation precedes Italian professional setup.
vera/new-client.request: Vera, organize this new client's intake and show what is still needed.
vera/new-client.scope: Fictional Italian case. Another working language does not enable a different professional country pack.
vera/new-client.basis: Received files establish documentary availability. Missing signature and declaration remain separate from proposed professional actions.
method: Prepare and classify the received documents, linking extraction and missing items to their sources.
Review and apply documentary decisions; promote only a coherent Italian handoff into the professional setup phase.
Prepare identity, engagement, privacy, AML and monitoring proposals with evidence and open points. The professional persists actual decisions through the review surfaces.
vera/new-client.conclusion: The extract and ID are available. Engagement is unsigned and ownership documentation is missing; the file is not declared complete.
vera/new-client.check: Receiving a document does not mean accepting its content. Workflow completion records delivery, not automatic client acceptance.
vera/new-client.question: The folder is named 'approved client'. Can we use that status?
vera/new-client.answer: No. Status comes from evidence and persisted decisions, not the folder name or its implied meaning.
vera/new-client.practice: Add the signed engagement letter and update affected proposals while retaining open AML issues.
vera/new-client.next: Select the actual client and received documents. A later focused AML review need not repeat all intake.

vera/open-item-reconciliation.title: A later payment explains the item, not the earlier balance
vera/open-item-reconciliation.goal: Verify open items at a cutoff while distinguishing subsequent events.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.scenario: At 30 June, the fictional schedule reports INV-701 open for EUR 1,000. Linked payments are EUR 600 on 28 June and EUR 400 on 5 July. The earlier payment has not been applied in the supplied open-item report.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.request: Vera, verify this item at 30 June and explain how to use the July payment.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.scope: Verification of a reported open population at a date. Invoices alone do not reconstruct outstanding balances.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.basis: O1 defines the reported population. Only B1 precedes the cutoff; the links from payments to the item require verification.
method: Confirm cutoff, client, population and totals. Obtain ledger and supporting evidence for the same engagement.
Compare amounts and relationships while separating candidates and reviewed decisions. Show cutoff balances, differences and later payments distinctly.
Present review items and persist actual decisions. Keep unresolved questions visible without automatically creating accounting entries.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.conclusion: If B1's relationship is confirmed, EUR 400 remains at 30 June. B2 documents later collection, not a retrospectively zero balance.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.check: The report date remains authoritative. A later receipt may corroborate recovery but does not rewrite history.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.question: Everything was collected by July. Can we show zero at 30 June?
vera/open-item-reconciliation.answer: No. The reviewed case has EUR 400 remaining at the cutoff. Show the July receipt as a subsequent event.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.practice: Move B2 to 29 June and rerun, checking which conclusion changes.
vera/open-item-reconciliation.next: Supply the open-item report at a precise date, accounting movements and relevant bank evidence.

vera/purchase-invoice-review.title: Connect each purchase invoice to the actual posting
vera/purchase-invoice-review.goal: Read population coverage and identify invoices needing accounting review.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.scenario: The fictional purchase batch has three invoices: one with a consistent posting, one with no posting found and one with two ambiguous candidates. Both the period and accounting population are explicitly bounded.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.request: Vera, check how this purchase-invoice batch connects to the actual accounting entries.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.scope: Review of supplied purchase invoices and postings. A missing link in this perimeter does not prove an invoice was never booked.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.basis: P1 is the XML batch and G1 the period's posting export. Findings stay bound to both perimeters; no missing posting is invented.
method: Import the invoice population and actual postings; qualify period, accounts, identities and batch totals.
Run the current matching and review method, including its required native capabilities. Leave unavailable stages pending instead of simulating them.
Read coverage, ambiguities and review proposals. The professional assesses expense nature and treatment; proposals do not become automatic postings or approvals.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.conclusion: One link is available, one is absent within scope and one is ambiguous. Preserve those distinctions through review.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.check: Matching coverage differs from accounting correctness. A successful technical run does not approve deductibility or VAT treatment.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.question: Can we state 'invoice not booked' without qualification for PA-102?
vera/purchase-invoice-review.answer: The supported finding is 'posting not found in the examined perimeter'. Check export completeness and period before a broader conclusion.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.practice: Add PA-102's posting and compare a fresh run without deleting the previous result.
vera/purchase-invoice-review.next: Select the purchase batch and actual period postings, and verify the installed workflow's required native capabilities.
